blockers.title: Point-in-time lockdown and kexec values do not prove that no prior kernel replacement occurred
evidence: runtimeContinuity observes four present-state facts: lockdown currently selects integrity, kexec_load_disabled is currently 1, no kexec image is currently loaded, and the current EFI BootCurrent value equals the boot-time value. None is a monotonic record that kexec was disabled continuously from the firmware handoff through observedAt.

kexec_load_disabled=1 prevents a later load in the current kernel lifetime; it does not establish that an earlier kernel did not load and execute M. After execution, M has no image staged, may set its own kexec_load_disabled to 1, may run in lockdown integrity when M is signed, and sees the same persistent BootCurrent. Every retained v29 value then has the required value.

A concrete passing trace is: firmware boots and measures package kernel K; K stages a different signed kernel M and executes it; M enables lockdown integrity and sets kexec_load_disabled=1 before qualification. kexec_loaded is 0 or absent because the staged image has already executed, and BootCurrent is unchanged. The fresh TPM quote still authenticates K's boot PCRs because kexec does not reset or extend them by this contract's procedure.

The subject remains exactly running-kernel-package and names K. No running-image digest, boot-epoch history, IMA/runtime measurement, DRTM state, or hardware-anchored no-transition indicator joins the executing M to kernelEvent. BootCurrent identifies the firmware boot option, not the currently executing image.

The reads are supplied through the running kernel itself. If M is adversarial rather than merely an older signed kernel, it can also falsify securityfs, procfs, and EFI-variable observations. The quote nonce is fresh, but none of these continuity values is a TPM statement about current code identity.
blockers.impact: The contract can issue a positive running-kernel-package attestation for K while M is executing. CLAUDE-V28-B1 therefore remains a false-allow blocker rather than being closed by the new runtimeContinuity object.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either narrow the subject to the firmware-launched kernel for this boot, or add an independently rooted current-execution measurement. A no-transition design must establish before any kernel replacement can be staged that every replacement path is disabled, bind that invariant to the boot attestation, and preserve it monotonically through observedAt; present-state sysctl reads are insufficient. Otherwise use a runtime measurement/appraisal or dynamic root whose authenticated state binds the current image bytes to kernelEvent.

blockers.title: The signed pre-kernel allowlist stops at K's LoadImage event and permits later firmware code before the separator
evidence: preKernelReferences.requiredFor and preKernelEventUnion.rule cover only events whose globalLogIndex is less than kernelEvent.globalLogIndex. kernelEvent is a LoadImage measurement, not a control-transfer boundary.

trustedHandoff.noInterveningPcr4Application forbids later EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION events before the first PCR-4 separator, but it does not forbid or allowlist EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_DRIVER, EV_EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES_DRIVER, firmware-blob, POST-code, IPL, or other code-bearing events after kernelEvent.

The PCR replay accepts every such later digest because it compares only the final reconstructed values to the quote. There is no comparison to an expected PCR transcript and no signedEntry requirement after the K event, so an unknown code digest can be genuine and still pass.

A passing global sequence is the authenticated PCR-4 boot-manager action, K's PCR-4 application measurement, an unknown driver D on its selected PCR, then the PCR-4 EV_SEPARATOR. The PCR-4 subsequence still has K as the unique next application and no other application violates noInterveningPcr4Application. D can execute after K is measured but before K receives control, hook the handoff, and launch M instead. D is outside the less-than-K allowlist cutoff.

The v29 runtime fields do not close this attack: M was selected during the firmware phase, not by post-boot kexec, so M can honestly report no loaded kexec image, kexec disabled, lockdown integrity, and the unchanged BootCurrent.
blockers.impact: Unknown pre-kernel code can execute after the selected K measurement and redirect control while the contract attests K as the running kernel. This preserves the LoadImage(K)-then-run(M) false allow through a sequence the new rules expressly permit.
blockers.requiredRepair: Extend the closed event union and signed-reference requirement through the first trusted control-transfer boundary, not merely to kernelEvent. Every code-bearing PCR-0/1/2/4 event after K and before the first applicable separator must either be forbidden or joined to a signed TCB member, including driver and firmware-blob types. State and verify that no later firmware code can execute between K's measurement and K's entry.

blockers.title: The code-versus-config exemption still trusts eventType even though eventType is not authenticated by the quoted PCR
evidence: The TPM replay extends event.digests[TPM_ALG_SHA256]. It does not extend eventType, the event-log encoding, or a domain tag. v29 nevertheless uses the prover-supplied eventType first to choose the preimage grammar and then to decide whether the digest is codeBearing and requires signedEntry or configBearing and is exempt.

Recomputing a digest from bytes authenticates those bytes, not their eventType. The listed grammars are not cryptographically domain-separated: arbitrary firmware/code bytes can also be formed as a valid tagged-event, handoff-table, or variable structure. An attacker choosing the measured bytes can construct such a polyglot without finding a SHA-256 collision.

A hostile prover can preserve the authentic PCR digest sequence for an unknown firmware blob X, relabel the log row as a known configBearing type, and supply X as that type's valid structure. The recomputed SHA-256 remains the quoted digest, but preKernelEventUnion now exempts the row from preKernelReferences. unknownTypeRefuses does not help because the selected type is known.

No signed expected transcript binds {pcrIndex, sequence position, eventType, digest}, and no firmware-authenticated event log binds the type label. The statement that preimage verification is required before reading eventType semantics is circular because the untrusted eventType selects the verifier used to justify those semantics.

The hidden X can execute before the boot-manager action, alter the later handoff, and leave the genuine action/K digest sequence intact. PCR reconstruction and all v29 joins then pass while an unsigned or unlisted TCB component controlled execution.
blockers.impact: An unknown code-bearing measurement can be downgraded to configBearing and bypass the signed TCB allowlist without changing any quoted PCR. PTCB-V28-B1/B2 are therefore not closed for adversarial event logs.
blockers.requiredRepair: Do not grant a no-signedEntry exemption from an eventType supplied only by the replay log. Bind type, PCR, order, and digest through a signed expected transcript or an authenticated measuring-agent log, or require a signed policy reference for every pre-kernel digest unless its type is independently authenticated. Define domain-separated typed measurements where the platform supports them; otherwise fail closed.

shouldFix.title: eventPreimage uses preimage and digest as the same value, yielding incompatible hash equations
evidence: eventPreimage.rule says SHA-256(type-specific preimage) must equal the event digest. The application rule then says the preimage is the PE/COFF Authenticode image digest, which is already the final SHA-256 image digest, while kernelEventSelection.match directly requires the event digest to equal that Authenticode digest. Literal application of both rules requires an unintended second SHA-256.

Several other entries are written as final operations rather than preimages, for example EV_EFI_PLATFORM_FIRMWARE_BLOB is described as SHA-256 of blob bytes. The global rule either hashes that result again or must silently mean something different for that type.

preKernelReferences.join says recomputedDigest MUST equal eventPreimage(event), but does not state recomputedDigest == event.digests[TPM_ALG_SHA256]. If eventPreimage(event) denotes raw bytes, the equality is type-invalid; if it denotes a final digest, the global SHA-256(preimage) rule is misnamed and the image rule conflicts with it.
No precedence clause selects one interpretation. A strict verifier rejects normal PE image events; permissive verifiers can choose different single-hash, double-hash, or row-join behavior.
shouldFix.impact: The new preimage repair is not reproducible and can fail closed on every in-scope Linux boot or be weakened differently by separate implementations.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define separate preimageBytes and recomputeDigest functions for each event type. Require recomputeDigest(eventType, preimageBytes) == event.digests[TPM_ALG_SHA256] == preKernelReferences.recomputedDigest. For PE image types, recomputeDigest is the Authenticode image-hash algorithm applied once to the exact image bytes; for ordinary blob types it is SHA-256 applied once to the exact blob bytes.

shouldFix.title: The RPM procedures still consume snapFd after the snapshot transition closes it
evidence: archiveSnapshot correctly opens roFd through /proc/self/fd, verifies identity/seals/digest, closes snapFd, and mandates that all later stages use only roFd.

preferredApi.headerBind still reads from snapFd; digest still preads snapFd; verify and extract still name rpmReadPackageFile on snapFd. cliInheritedFd.noWritableCopy likewise says children consume the sealed snapFd.

Those live branch-specific statements conflict with preferredApi.open/hold and cliInheritedFd.handoff, which use roFd, and with the global step that has already closed snapFd. There is no precedence rule making the stale names non-normative.
shouldFix.impact: A literal producer uses a closed descriptor and refuses every RPM qualification; a permissive producer must guess that each snapFd token means roFd. The O_RDONLY repair is structurally present but not executable consistently.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace every post-transition snapFd reference in headerBind, digest, verify, extract, and CLI consumption with roFd. Reserve snapFd exclusively for the creation/sealing/reopen transition and state that use after close refuses.

shouldFix.title: EV_NO_ACTION is declared non-extending but the replay algorithm extends every Event2 row
evidence: eventPreimage.EV_NO_ACTION says no PCR extend, and preKernelEventUnion explicitly permits EV_NO_ACTION before kernelEvent.

replayAlgorithm.step has no event-type exception: for each TCG_PCR_EVENT2 on a reconstructed PCR it computes SHA-256(old || event digest). It therefore extends a row the same contract says must not extend.

The all-zero initialization also supplies no declared handling for an EV_NO_ACTION startup-locality record. Even without that special case, the direct extend-versus-no-extend conflict makes the same retained log replay two ways.
shouldFix.impact: Any permitted Event2 EV_NO_ACTION entry can make the reconstructed PCR disagree with the genuine quote, causing systematic over-refusal or validator divergence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give replay an explicit event-type state machine: skip non-extending EV_NO_ACTION rows, define any startup-locality initialization semantics, and state exactly which encoded log records participate in each PCR extension. Add a replay vector containing EV_NO_ACTION.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 3 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v29 adds the intended event-preimage vocabulary, closed event union, runtime indicators, O_RDONLY memfd reopen, and unambiguous PCR-4 indices, while preserving prior TPM and RPM repairs. It still cannot prove K is currently running: a completed kexec leaves every continuity value passing; the signed allowlist omits code loaded after K's LoadImage event; and the code/config exemption trusts an eventType absent from the quoted PCR preimage. The preimage equations, post-transition descriptor names, and EV_NO_ACTION replay are also inconsistent. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
